capex.item: Data centre capex expected at about Rs 4,200 crore (USD 600 million) with a target business plan capacity of 300 MW.

capex.item: Cell and module line capacity expansion to 3.5 GW will be completed in Q2 FY2023.
capex.quote: the cell and modular line capacity expansion to 3.5 gigawatt will be completed in Q2 FY2023

capex.item: The new 2 GW Mono PERC solar cell and module plant at Mundra (MSEL) is likely to be commissioned in Q2 FY2023, within about six months.
capex.quote: The entire facility solar cells and solar photovoltaic panels of this plant is likely to be commissioned in Q2 FY2023 in the coming six months.

capex.item: Expects to reach full or near completion on three HAM road projects (Bilaspur, Suryapet, Mancherial) in FY2023 with about Rs 1,900 crore of remaining project cost, plus near completion of Vijayawada (Rs 1,248 crore project, ~20% complete).
capex.quote: we would expect to start completing or reach full completion on approximately four of our projects and more likely three out of four near completing and all three would be the HAM projects Bilaspur, Suryapet and Mancherial

capex.item: The FY24 capex splits as roughly USD 300 million green hydrogen, USD 1.1 billion airports, USD 1.7 billion roads, just under USD 100 million water, just under USD 200 million data centre and just under USD 200 million copper completion.
capex.quote: Approximately about $300 million for Green Hydrogen, $1.1 billion for airports, approximately $1.7 billion for the road network, just under $100 million for water, just under $200 million for the Data Center, and then small completion cost for the copper project just under $200 million.

capex.item: Airport capex will be about USD 1.1 billion in FY24 (at Rs 80/USD) and will broadly remain in that range next year before declining once phase-1 of the airport development plan is complete.
capex.quote: about US $1.1 billion this year would be the CAPEX on airport. It will broadly remain in that range for the next year then there will be decline

capex.item: Production of the 5.2 MW prototype-1 wind turbine (provisional certificate received) is expected during Q2FY24, and an update on the ingot and wafer facility will be given with the half-yearly results.
capex.quote: the integrated manufacturing division received the provisional certificate of 5.2-megawatt prototype-1 wind turbine. Production of this is expected during this quarter.

capex.item: Four of the ten road projects have crossed 50% completion and are stated to be right on schedule.
capex.quote: For Road portfolio during this quarter, 4 of our 10 road projects have achieved over 50% completion and are right on schedule.

capex.item: Three of the 10 HAM/BOT road projects will be completed within FY24, and the majority of the remaining projects (excluding Ganga Expressway) in FY25.
capex.quote: out of our 10 projects that we have on stream today plus the BOT assets and one TOT project, three of the HAM projects will be completed within this financial year

capex.item: The 2GW ingot-wafer plant is scheduled to be commissioned by the end of FY24, with the first wafer in India already produced.
capex.quote: The 2GW of ingot wafer plant is scheduled to be commissioned by the end of this financial year.

capex.item: Company expects to start the open cut / box cut at the Dhirauli commercial coal block within FY24 once FC Stage-1 and Stage-2 approvals come through, with coal only from the following year.

capex.item: Four of the seven commercial blocks are underground mines (Bijahan, Gondkhari, Gondulpara and others) and will take until 2025-2026 to be prepared for coal production.

capex.quote: Copper project is on schedule for first calendar quarter next year. We pretty much, it's just right on schedule.

capex.item: Navi Mumbai International Airport will be completed on the committed December 2024 timeline despite the heavy monsoon.
capex.quote: We committed to complete, we will complete as committed.

bull_bear.body: The 33% solar margins are not just from cost savings but from vertical integration and export pricing power; MDO's near-zero inventory implies contractually locked-in demand, making volumes highly predictable; Green hydrogen is being built as a portfolio of cash-positive modules, not a subsidized bet; Navi Mumbai Airport’s schedule is critical for Mumbai’s airport congestion relief — a systemic national infrastructure win
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- AEL raised Rs. 15,000 cr in July 2026 through India's largest QIP by a non-financial corporate, bid 3.8x the base issue size by domestic mutual funds and long-only global FIIs; promoter shareholding stands revised to 71.97% post issue.
- The stated capital management plan is aligned to the underlying business philosophy, with consolidated net debt/equity at 0.85x in Q1-27 and a value-unlocking model of incubating businesses and demerging them into separate listed entities.
- Credit metrics as of Q1-27: net external debt/EBITDA at 3.3x (versus 3.9x in FY26 and a 5.2x peak in FY22), debt service coverage 2.0x and interest coverage 2.6x.
- Consolidated gross debt stood at Rs. 97,622 cr as at Jun-26 (Rs. 86,491 cr long-term plus Rs. 11,131 cr working capital), with net external debt of Rs. 73,998 cr after netting shareholder loans of Rs. 13,640 cr and cash of Rs. 9,984 cr; airports (Rs. 32,843 cr), roads (Rs. 18,024 cr) and copper (Rs. 10,542 cr) carry the largest segment debt.
- Funding is deliberately diversified across private banks (22%), USD bonds (22%), global international banks (24%), PSU banks (9%), NBFCs/FIs (3%) and DII (1%), under an infrastructure financing framework covering duration matching and rate/currency risk.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Group 'incubator' model: AEL has a demonstrated track record of incubating early-stage infrastructure businesses and scaling them into industry-leading, separately-listed entities (Adani Ports & SEZ, Adani Energy Solutions, Adani Power, Adani Green Energy, Adani Total Gas), giving it a repeatable playbook for entering new high-growth sectors such as the new energy ecosystem, airports, data centers, roads, copper and PVC
- Backward-integrated New Energy value chain: ANIL is building in-house electrolyser manufacturing at Mundra (including its own Electrolyser Testing Laboratory), which the Company states strengthens quality control, optimises costs, and supports higher-performance electrolysers versus sourcing components externally
- Adani Solar has a proven execution track record, strong customer relationships and process-driven manufacturing, positioning it as a trusted supplier to both domestic and export markets; it was an early adopter of TOPCon cell technology in India and operates high-efficiency automated mono PERC (up to 23.2%) and TOPCon (average 25.3%) cell lines
- Cross-group infrastructure integration: the Company describes an ability to import fuel through group-owned ports, feed group mining output into power generation, move power over an extensive group-owned transmission grid, and locate data-centre cable-landing stations within group-owned ports with land secured via the group's real-estate arm
- Policy-linked cost/demand support: ANIL was awarded SECI Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) support for domestic electrolyser manufacturing capacity, and Adani Solar benefits from India's Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) ecosystem plus captive demand from within the Adani Group
- Diversified, predominantly B2B customer base spanning Integrated Resources Management, Mining Services, New Energy, Defence & Aerospace, Data Centers and Copper, complemented by B2C exposure through Airports and Roads
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Chronic physical climate risk — heat stress — Rising temperatures reduce equipment efficiency, accelerate infrastructure degradation, and increase maintenance needs; higher cooling demand raises energy consumption and operating costs; prolonged heat exposure lowers worker productivity and raises heat-related illness/safety risk.
- Acute physical climate risk — excess rainfall and floods — Heavy rainfall/flooding disrupts power and communication services, slows production, delays movement of raw materials and finished goods via blocked/flooded roads, and water stagnation/contamination raises health risks for workers.
- Climate transition risk (regulatory, technology, legal, market, reputational) — Company's TCFD/IFRS S2-aligned scenario analysis (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP5-8.5, Current Policies, Net Zero 2050) explicitly assesses transition risk across current and emerging regulation, technology, legal, market, and reputational categories over short (2030), medium (2030-2050) and long (2050+) term horizons, though the routed text names the categories without elaborating specific impacts.

business.body:
- AEL is the flagship incubator of the Adani Group, with a stated model of building emerging infrastructure businesses and then divesting them into separate listed entities; it has already spun out APSEZ, Adani Power and AESL (2015) and AGEL and Adani Total Gas (2018).
- The portfolio is deliberately split into 'Established' businesses (mining services, IRM, mining, metals and industrials) that provide stability and 'Incubating' core-infra businesses (ANIL ecosystem, AdaniConneX data centres, airports, roads) that provide growth.
- Management frames a repeatable, proven investment model spanning origination, development (Adani Infra India, Cemindia, PSP Projects), operations (AIMSL) and centralised capital management, plugged into a group core-infra platform serving a 375 mn userbase.
- The deck cites 31.5% shareholder-value CAGR over 30 years and a market cap of USD 41.6 bn as of June 30, 2026, alongside group assets such as India's largest commercial port (Mundra), Asia's longest private HVDC line and the world's largest renewable cluster (Khavda).
- The next incubation wave is explicitly centred on the green hydrogen ecosystem, airport management, data centres, roads and primary industries (copper, PVC), all described as having significant scope for value unlocking.

- [Governance] The board has 50% independent directors and 12.5% women directors, with the Audit and Nomination & Remuneration Committees 100% independent and a Risk Management Committee running dedicated M&A, legal/regulatory/tax, commodity price risk and reputation risk sub-committees; statutory auditors are Shah Dhandharia & Co. business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Adani Enterprises Limited incubates and nurtures emerging infrastructure businesses that contribute to nation-building and economic growth, having previously scaled and separately listed industry-leading entities including Adani Ports & SEZ, Adani Energy Solutions, Adani Power, Adani Green Energy and Adani Total Gas. Its current portfolio spans Integrated Resources Management (mineral procurement & logistics), the New Energy Ecosystem (green hydrogen and derivatives, solar cells/modules, wind turbine generators and electrolysers via wholly-owned subsidiary Adani New Industries Limited), Copper smelting and refining, Airport and Road construction/operation/maintenance, Commercial Mining, Mining Services (Mine Development & Operations), and Defence & Aerospace manufacturing. The Company and its subsidiaries primarily serve B2B customers across Integrated Resources Management, Mining Services, New Energy Ecosystem, Defence & Aerospace, Data Centers and Copper, while operating a B2C model for its Airports and Road businesses; the next phase of investment is focused on high-growth sectors including the new energy ecosystem, airport management, data centers, roads, and primary industries like copper and PVC.

outlook.body:
- Pursuing twin strategic engines — 'Accelerating Infrastructure, Leveraging Intelligence' — integrating physical infrastructure (energy, transport, logistics, utilities, industrial manufacturing) with digital/AI capabilities (automation, predictive systems, real-time analytics) rather than treating them as separate priorities.
- Building a single unified, vertically-integrated infrastructure-to-execution platform (own mining, generation, ports/import, transmission, real estate, project/construction/design teams) instead of scattered standalone businesses, positioned as the basis of competitive advantage.
- Maintaining continued, counter-cyclical capital investment through global volatility on the stated belief that 'India's future cannot wait', rather than pausing amid geopolitical/energy-security uncertainty.
- Implementing a three-layer organisational structure intended to flatten hierarchy, strip away 'legacy corporate structure' bureaucracy, and give portfolio-wide visibility and faster decision-making ('designed for the AI era').
- Operating a 'Partner Management Model' that treats external execution partners as an extension of the organisation to scale delivery and standardise best practices across projects.
- Building an internal leadership pipeline by nurturing talent from within ('Adani DNA') as a meritocracy-based succession strategy to manage continued growth.
- Applying a 'Worker Dignity Model' focused on frontline workforce welfare as a stated enabler of execution quality at the project 'last mile'.
- Entering nuclear energy as a new strategic vertical (via Adani Atomic Energy Limited, a Group entity referenced in the Chairman's letter) framed as securing India's long-term energy independence.
- IRM (IntegratedResources Management) segment: building a multi-commodity sourcing/trading portfolio and pursuing partnerships with miners, with the stated aim of becoming a global leader in natural-resource trading (beyond the current coal-import focus); expanded into retail via the 'Adani IRM Portal'.
- Mining Services (MDO) segment: strategic focus on expanding the natural-resources business, diversifying into other profitable mining segments, supporting mine owners in maximising reserves, and full-scale digitalisation of operations to improve efficiency and sustainability.
- Roads segment (ARTL): expanding beyond road/highway construction into metro and rail projects, building on eight years of HAM/BOT/TOT execution experience.
- Petrochemicals segment (Mundra Petrochemicals Limited): developing a PVC project intended to reduce India's import dependence, framed as aligned with the national self-reliance ('self-reliance') agenda; selected the carbide-acetylene production route.
- Copper segment (Kutch Copper Limited): positioning as a key player in India's copper self-reliance by leveraging Group infrastructure, resource-trading and energy expertise, and the plant's coastal/rail/road connectivity for supply-chain efficiency.
- The routed text does not contain an explicit stated dividend/payout or reinvestment policy. The Notice of AGM records a routine ordinary-business item to declare a dividend on equity shares for FY2025-26 (no payout ratio or philosophy disclosed). Separately, the 'Dividend Distribution Policy' section of the source (as routed) opens into Financial Highlights and a 'Credit Rating' sub-heading stating the Company's 'financial discipline and prudence is reflected in the strong credit rating,' but the text is cut off before naming the rating or describing the underlying capital-allocation approach.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: AEL's growth capex is concentrated in its New Energy Ecosystem (ANIL), Data Centers (AdaniConneX/ACX), Water (AWL) and 'incubating' core infra businesses (Airports/AAHL, Roads/ARTL, Copper/KCL, PVC/MPL, and coal mining). In New Energy: ANIL commissioned India's first off-grid 5 MW Green Hydrogen Pilot Plant in Kutch, Gujarat in June 2025, powered by solar with battery storage, described as a proof of concept for ANIL's upcoming New Energy Hub at Mundra, Gujarat; ANIL targets a Green Hydrogen production capacity of 1 MMTPA (equivalent to 5.6 MMTPA of Green Ammonia) by 2030, in line with the National Green Hydrogen Mission. ANIL is also building an integrated electrolyser manufacturing ecosystem at Mundra designed for 5 GW of electrolysers annually, and has been awarded a SECI PLI incentive for 300 MW of annual electrolyser manufacturing capacity (Tranche I & II). In solar manufacturing, Adani Solar currently operates 4 GW of cell capacity, 4 GW of module capacity and 2 GW of ingot-wafer capacity; an additional 6 GW of TOPCon cell and 6 GW of module capacity is under construction and planned for commissioning in FY 2026-27, taking cumulative capacity to 10 GW of cells and 10 GW of modules as part of a fully automated solar manufacturing ecosystem at Mundra. In wind, ANIL offers four WTG models (2.25 GW manufacturing capacity), secured external orders for 300 MW under its 3.3 MW platform, and supplied 231 WTG sets (including 51 of the 3.3 MW model) during the year, with plans to expand into new domestic and international regions. In Data Centers, AdaniConneX (a 50:50 JV between Adani Enterprises and EdgeConneX) has a cumulative order book of 560+ MW, of which 55+ MW is operational across Chennai, Noida, Hyderabad and Pune; it completed and handed over 19.2 MW of capacity to hyperscale customers during the year, with facilities under development at four locations progressing on schedule, and it announced a partnership with Google to develop India's largest AI Data Center campus in Visakhapatnam. ACX targets 2 GW of renewable-powered, tied-up Data Center capacity by 2030 and is expanding hyperscale campuses in Pune, Noida and Hyderabad. The Water business, run through wholly-owned subsidiary Adani Water Limited (AWL), is positioned in wastewater treatment, irrigation infrastructure, river interlinking, large-scale water supply/distribution and desalination projects, though the provided text does not disclose specific AWL projects, capacities or timelines. Among core infra businesses driving the rise in net external debt, the Company cited: commencement of operations at the greenfield Navi Mumbai International Airport; inauguration of the integrated new terminal building at Guwahati airport, alongside a proposed expansion of Guwahati's LGBIA to 18 MPPA passenger handling and 0.15 MTPA cargo handling capacity (EIA conducted, dated 04-Sep-2025); an amendment to the environmental clearance for non-operational (landside) area development at Mumbai's CSMIA; completion of the greenfield Ganga Expressway project and three HAM road assets; construction of a 500 KTPA Copper plant (KCL) with production now ramping up; and construction of a 1 MMTPA PVC plant (MPL). Management stated that EBITDA from these under-construction/ramping assets is expected to be unlocked from the next fiscal year (FY27). Separately, in natural resources, the Company/its group entities obtained environmental clearance (15-04-2025) for the Gondbahera Ujheni Underground Coal mine (4.12/6.18 MTPA normative/peak capacity, Madhya Pradesh) and clearance was recommended (EAC meeting, Sept 2025) for the adjacent Gondbahera Ujheni East Coal Mine.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Chairman's letter frames AI/data-centre growth as structurally driving demand for energy, transmission and physical infrastructure ('Before AI can think, energy must flow; before data can move, infrastructure must stand'), underpinning the Group's capital allocation toward energy + data-centre-adjacent infrastructure.
- Airports segment (fragment only, section start not captured in routed text): 'With diversified revenue streams, economies of scale, and substantial organic growth potential, the Airports segment remains a pivotal contributor to the Company's long-term growth trajectory' over the next 2-3 years.
- Roads industry: Union Budget 2026-27 allocated Rs. 3.09 lakh crore to the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (+8% YoY); NHAI constructed 5,313 km of national highways in FY26; highway project execution is expected to accelerate further, supported by Gati Shakti, Bharatmala Pariyojana, the National Infrastructure Pipeline, and revisions to the Model Concession Agreement for HAM projects.
- Roads (ARTL) outlook: with completion of the largest greenfield project (Ganga Expressway), ARTL 'is poised to significantly increase its profitability'; with commencement of the majority of projects, revenue/EBITDA are expected to 'remain stable during the concession period'.
- IRM/coal industry: domestic coal production is estimated to reach 1,210-1,220 MT by FY 2029-30 (from 1,048 MT in FY25); demand from the power and industrial sectors 'continues to outpace supply', sustaining coking/non-coking coal import reliance despite government measures (Single Window Clearance, MMDR Act amendments allowing captive mines to sell up to 50% of output, 100% FDI under automatic route) aimed at boosting domestic production.
- Copper industry: India copper demand grew 9.3% YoY to 1,878 KT in FY 2024-25 (24.1% CAGR over FY20-25), driven by renewables (India's 500 GW renewable-capacity target by 2030), metro-rail/railway electrification, and urbanisation/housing/EV-infrastructure growth — cited as sustaining domestic copper demand.
- Petrochemicals/PVC industry: India's PVC demand-supply gap is estimated at ~2.5 MTPA (demand ~4.3 MTPA vs domestic supply of 1.8 MTPA); India is projected to become one of the largest PVC producers by 2027; demand is expected to be supported by Smart Cities, Housing for All, AMRUT, Jal Jeevan Mission and Swachh Bharat Mission infrastructure programmes.
- Mining Services (MDO) outlook: 'As India's largest MDO, the Company aims to increase volume by 20% in next year', with a stated 'clear long runway available for growth' from its expanded service-contract portfolio; growth is expected to be driven by full-scale digitalisation of operations.
- IRM outlook: business focussed on 'enhancing its capabilities and reach by building a multi-commodity portfolio' and actively seeking partnerships with miners to ensure 'timely and cost-effective resource delivery', aiming for 'long-term sustainable growth'.
- Adani Energy Solutions Limited (Group entity referenced in Chairman's letter): transmission order book rose from Rs. 59,936 crore to Rs. 71,779 crore in FY26; secured major projects including the Khavda-South Olpad HVDC line, and commissioned Mumbai's first VSC-based HVDC project.
- ARTL (Roads) portfolio increased to 20 projects (11 HAM, 5 BOT, 3 TOT, 1 ropeway) after adding six new projects during the year, including the Kedarnath-Son Prayag ropeway project; 13 projects are now operational following commencement of the Ganga Expressway.
- Mining Services portfolio expanded to 18 service contracts with peak capacity of 145.4 MMT per annum; the GP-II mine MDO contract (peak capacity 23.6 MMT per annum) was made operational during the year, taking the operational-contract count to seven.
- A binding MoU was signed with Google for a gigawatt-scale data centre in Visakhapatnam, cited as reflecting global technology-leader confidence in the Group's infrastructure platform.

deepdive.thesis: Adani Enterprises is rapidly scaling an integrated infrastructure and green energy ecosystem, with incubating businesses now contributing nearly half of EBITDA, driven by domestic manufacturing breakthroughs in solar, wind, and green hydrogen, while leveraging its mining and logistics moat to fund capital-intensive transitions. The company is on track to become a vertically integrated clean energy powerhouse with global export potential.
